b.em: Services to be delivered by Primus Auditing Operations

div.p:
Estimated Travel Expenses: - Travel expenses are estimated and are subject to change based on actual travel expenses incurred.
Travel expenses are on a direct reimbursement basis and include all expenses for transportation, accommodation and meals. Whenever possible, trips are combined with other business and expenses are divided to reduce the total costs for all of Primus Auditing Ops' customers.

If any information or data provided by Customer or on Customer's behalf pursuant to this Agreement is incomplete or inaccurate, Primus Auditing Ops will not be responsible in any way for deficiencies in the services.

1. DELIVERY. The Audit Report and Corrective Action Plan Report (“CAPR”) are shared through the Supplier Ethical Data Exchange (“SEDEX”) platform. The Corrective Action Plan (“CAPR”) that is sign in the closing meeting of the audit is a preliminary summary of findings which may be subject to change during the technical review by the Primus Auditing Ops quality team.
The Audit Services process consists of a sampling exercise only and does not guarantee that the audited site prior, during or post-audit, is in full compliance with Your Requirements, laws or industry or international standards. The Audit Services do not involve any assessment or evaluation to independent safety certification standards, and our affiliates and we have no responsibility to make any independent safety assessment. The Audit Services process represents an evaluation based on specific points in time and includes include any or all of the following: records review, worker interviews, management interviews, and visual observation of sites.

2. TRANSFER OF DATA TO OUTSIDE PARTIES. Primus Auditing Ops may be required to submit information obtained during the audit to either Supplier SEDEX and/or to the Association of Professional Social Compliance Auditors (“APSCA”) for its authorized use. By executing this Agreement, Customer acknowledges that such information may be provided to the applicable SEDEX and/or APSCA, and consents to the transfer of such information. We may retain a copy of the Audit Report and other materials for our archives. All information and material gathered in the execution of the Audit Services is retained for our use.

3. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY. Customer hereby releases Primus Auditing Ops, its employees, directors, principals, agents, and affiliates, from any loss or liability suffered by Customer, resulting from services performed under this Agreement. Such release shall include any actual, incidental, consequential or other damages beyond amounts paid to Primus Auditing Ops for auditing performed and/or facilitated by Primus Auditing Ops. Customer further acknowledges and agrees that Primus Auditing Ops' liability is limited only to the audit work performed by it, and the parties expressly acknowledge that Primus Auditing Ops is not liable for Customer's commodity, its safety, or quality.

4. GOVERNING LAW / VENUE. For audit services conducted in the United States, this Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of California, and in the event that it is necessary to institute any action to enforce any right granted herein or to redress any alleged breach hereof, then the exclusive venue for such action shall reside with the Superior Court located in Santa Maria, California. For audit services conducted outside the United States, this Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the country where the audit service is provided.

5. RIGHT TO REFERRAL. Customer acknowledges that Primus Auditing Ops is, or may, contract out the auditing services performed for Customer. Because an independent auditor is engaged in his/her own independent contracting business and is not an employee of Primus Auditing Ops, if Primus Auditing Ops refers the audit out to a contractor, it will not obtain insurance (professional liability, workers' compensation, general liability, auto, etc.) for the auditor. Independent auditors agree by a separate referral agreement to obtain his/her own insurance coverage and furnish a copy of the certificate of insurance to Primus Auditing Ops. Furthermore, in those instances in which an independent auditor is retained, Primus Auditing Ops will be acting in the sole capacity of independent contractor and any information or data received will be merely transmitted between parties, making no independent judgment, representations or warranties as to the facts, observations or inferences made relative to same.

6. AUDIT AND SURVEILLANCE. Customer agrees and acknowledges Free access must be provided for all scheduled audits, as well as any potential random quality assurance checks (depending on the audit scheme's requirements) of customer's operation including but not limited to: examination of documentation, interview with workers, taking photographs as part of audit evidence, records, and access to the equipment, location(s), area(s), personnel, and full physical inspection of Customer's subcontractors. The confidentiality of all proprietary information will be respected. Technologies and/or unique processes of Customer's operation will not be disclosed. In countries where there are data protection requirements (for example, all countries in the European Union), all said requirements shall be complied with. Customer agrees to allow observers from Primus Auditing Ops and/or varying governing bodies if the customer's audit or certification is randomly selected for surveillance for quality assurance purposes. Customer further agrees to grant free access in order to verify continued compliance with the scheme guidelines. Customer acknowledges complaints related to compliance must be documented, and subsequent investigation of complaints is possible, and in some cases may be mandatory. Documentation of complaints and investigation may be subject to inspection during audit or surveillance or at the request or Primus Auditing Ops at any time. Customer acknowledges that its failure to fully comply with this section, either during the time of audit or until the report is submitted in the platform, is a material breach of this agreement and can result in an investigation involving the scheme owner due to lack of information or clarification due to the resulting complaint. In the case of audits managed through the SEDEX platform, if there is a breach of this section, the guidelines outlined in the Sedex Members Ethical Trade Audit (“SMETA”) audit protocol will be followed. Customer understands and agrees to perform Follow-up Audits when corrective actions cannot be verified in a desk review, for example, in the event of critical non-compliances and/or requiring the validation of corrective actions through worker testimony. During the follow-up audit, a sample of interviews and record reviews will be conducted. The sample size for these reviews will be determined based on the nature of the corrective actions being verified.

Customer should be aware that the number of interviews and records may increase during the audit at the auditor's request, depending on the situation. This is in accordance with SEDEX's established guidelines to ensure an unbiased assessment with sufficient information to comply with audit guidelines.

The Audit Report does not confirm or certify compliance with industry or international laws or standards. The Audit Report is derived solely through sampling, which includes document sampling, individual sampling for interviews, and area sampling for observation. This sampling activity does not guarantee that the audited facility fully complies with the audited requirements. The Audit Report does not include on-site testing of equipment, assessment of building safety, code compliance, or evaluation of independent safety certification standards. Audit services are reported based on the limited audit scope of laws and regulations. Some laws and regulations may not be available to the auditor.

7. CUSTOMER OBLIGATIONS. Customer agrees to comply with the points cited in the SMETA audit, under the Ethical Trading Initiative Base Code (“ETI Base Code”), as well as the applicable local Laws. Any deviation detected during the audit will be reported and indicated during the closing meeting and in the corresponding document (CAPR), for which Customer must take corrective actions to cure the deviation, and is responsible for entering them into the SEDEX platform Customer's corrective actions, as well as entering them into the SEDEX platform is the sole responsibility of the Customer, to which Customer acknowledges, understands, and agrees. A review of corrective actions may be requested by Customer either before or after the audit, and may be subject to a separate quote and service agreement (“Corrective Action Review”).

In the event that a new on-site visit is required to verify corrective actions as determined in the closing meeting of the corresponding audit, the Customer agrees in advance to pay all costs related to said visit, namely travel expenses, mileage, auditor and administrative expenses. Primus Auditing Operations, for this purpose, will send an individual quote accordingly.

Customer further agrees to comply with the following conditions:
a. In the following circumstances, Customer agrees to provide:
Initial Audit: Records for the last 12 months, unless the site is newly established (3 months).
Periodic Audit:
• At least 3 months' records after the previous audit month.
Auditor may check:
• Interval from previous audit >= 12 months: previous 12 months' records
• Interval from the previous audit < 12 months: from the month after the previous audit to the most recent full month.
Follow-Up audits:
• At least 2 months' records after the previous audit month, if “Wage” or “Hour” corrective actions are required to verify.
Auditor may check:
• From the month after the previous audit to the most recent full month.
Desktop Follow up: N/A - ”Wage” and “Hour” issues cannot be verified by desktop.
Notification of an Audit, for unannounced or semi-announced audits, shall follow the periods established by the scheme owner, Primus Auditing Operations requirements or client specific requirements. The most stringent requirement will apply as applicable.
If have any doubt as to the type of audit, consult the scheme owner's documents as well as the Buyer's requirements of you or your Client and/or with the requester of the audit. Primus Auditing Ops is not responsible for the Client's failure to provide information regarding the Buyer's requirements, including; Type of audit, version, nature, scope, seasonal period or date the audit is requested. Primus Auditing Ops will perform the audit service in accordance with the details provided in the application form and Self-Assessment Questionnaire (“SAQ”).
Audits shall be undertaken during a period of high employment numbers of at least 60% of the workforce, and when the employment site is in full operation (such as peak production or harvest).
If the audit is completed at less than 80% of peak workforce, but more than 60%, this shall be clearly explained, with a reason given, within the audit report. Audits shall not take place during low season or below 60% of the peak workforce.
Sedex does not determine how often sites should undertake social audits, however, Sedex does require sites to have the following available documentation before undertaking a SMETA audit.
If the above is not met, the applicant must submit written agreements that the audit applicant (buyer-client) approves, i.e., that the site is audited outside of peak season or at least 60% of the workforce.
For larger audits, an audit team may be needed. The client agrees that the audit may be conducted with an audit team.
For the purpose of evaluating the continuous improvement system as a mandatory requirement of Sedex towards Primus Auditing Operations, in the audit service may be selected to perform an audit evaluation of the auditor, where this is the case, the site will not be responsible for any additional charges or travel expenses of the evaluator, the evaluator does not participate in the audit exercise and does not intervene in the results of the audit.
Based on the information provided on the audit request form, it is possible that a translator/interpreter may be required, the translator/interpreter will be chosen by Primus Auditing Operations and the costs of the translator/interpreter will be borne by the audit requestor. May be included in the scope and the auditor's time shall be accounted for.
Customer must deliver the Self-Assessment Questionnaire (“SAQ”) or the site profile format prior to the service quotation or at least 5 days prior to the date of the onsite visit/ audit. The site is responsible for providing this information; otherwise, there may be changes in the audit cost, and/or it may not be executed due to failure to complete the requested pre-information in SEDEX. Likewise, the requesting company must provide the ZC and ZS registration numbers to Primus Auditing Ops at least 10 days before the audit, otherwise the audit will be rescheduled and the per diem payment is subject to the assigned auditor having made any expenses prior to the audit cancellation either by Customer or due to lack of registration on the SEDEX platform.
Customer is responsible for preparing the audit information which includes access to records, documentation, facilities and everything that is necessary to verify compliance with the regulations and requirements pursuant to SMETA Customer is responsible for compliance with SMETA and the guidelines of the ETI Base Code, undertakes to carry out all the activities necessary to maintain compliance after the audit, as well as the implementation of measures consistent with the continuous improvement in accordance with the conditions reflected in the Audit Report.
Customer agrees to inform Primus Auditing Ops of any change in the operation that may affect the Customer's ability to comply with the audit requirements or that generates a significant change in the way the Customer performs its activities. Likewise, any changes must be updated by the audited site in the SAQ or the site profile format
Customer agrees to apply the corrective actions within the time period agreed to during the closing meeting with the auditor. In the event that it is unable to apply or otherwise the corrective actions, it will submit the situation in writing to both Primus Auditing Ops and the auditor.
Customer agrees to act in good faith and inform Primus Auditing Operations in writing of any significant change that contravenes the provisions of the ETI Base Code evaluated.
Customer agrees to have representatives from senior management, managers responsible for key functions (for example HR and production) and trade unions / workers' representatives at the time of the onsite audit.
Customer agrees to give the auditor full access to the applicable audited operation, documents and personnel during the onsite visit in order to perform the SMETA audit.
If an auditor has Full Access Denied, the auditor shall trigger an alert in all cases. If the auditor is able to enter the site but cannot access any of the necessary information, they shall raise an alert and a Non-Compliance.
If an auditor has Partial Access Denied, the auditor shall continue with the audit, but raise a Non-Compliance with a detailed description of the issue(s).
If homeworking exists, Primus Auditing Ops shall include a review of homeworkers in the scope of the audit; the preference is for a home visit to be arranged if this is not possible, the auditor can include a review of their payments and contract. Primus Auditing Ops shall communicated with the audit requestor to extend the number of days to accommodate the home visits.
Primus Auditing Ops have policies in place that allow for night shift workers to be included in the audit either via early start or late finish times on one audit day, or additional visit to conduct site tour and interviews at night. While night shift workers may be included in day shift interviews, visits during the night shift are most valuable to ensure the full range of interviewees are available for selection, and the night work can be observed via site tour. If night shift visits are not conducted, documentation relating to these workers shall be included in the sample.
In the event of a change, due to information not previously declared by Customer (for example, an increase in workers, dormitories at remote distances, among others that imply the auditor needs to allocate more audit days than originally scheduled) during the audit, and this results in modifications to the audit duration, the auditor must immediately inform Primus Auditing Ops. Primus Auditing Ops will then communicate the next steps to Customer. Under no circumstances should Customer arrange directly with the auditor. Additionally, Primus Auditing Ops may cancel or reschedule the audit without liability, and the expenses incurred during the audit where changes were detected must be covered by Customer, including the audit cost.
Any accommodation arranged for workers by the audited facility, either directly or through third parties, regardless of whether it is owned or licensed commercially, may be within the scope of the SMETA audit. Where such accommodation is within or adjacent to the perimeter, it shall be included in the audit included in the SMETA audit. Otherwise in the audit request and will be included in the schedule and report. Such external accommodation may be included in the scope and the auditor's time shall be accounted for. If access to the accommodation is not permitted, the auditor may include it as part of the audit findings and in the audit report.

8. AUDIT RESULTS. Customer must comply with the following:
Customer agrees to always comply with the requirements of the SMETA methodology.
Customer shall comply by implementing the appropriate changes when communicated through Primus Auditing Ops to the Customer.
Customer acknowledges that it cannot make assertions regarding the audit results that are inconsistent with the scope of the audit performed. Furthermore, Customer may not use the audit results in a misleading or unauthorized manner, or in a manner that damages the reputation of Primus Auditing Ops. In addition, Customer acknowledges that the times for closing non-conformities should be discussed during the closing of the audit with the auditor so that they are established in the CAPR.
The client will have access to the final audit report and summary of findings only through the Sedex platform.
Primus Auditing Operations will upload the audit report within 20 working days on the Sedex platform.
The customer is responsible for publishing the audit through the Sedex platform and establishing customer relationships through their portal so that their buyer or audit requester has access to the audit information. Please refer to the supplier manual and Sedex E-Learning documents to upload corrective actions on the portal.
Primus Auditing Ops does not issue any certificate or document other than the Audit Report and CAPR.
After concluding the service, Primus Auditing Ops may retain a copy of all documents related to the audit for as long as Primus Auditing Ops deems appropriate based on the needs required for follow-up and/or as evidence of the assessment conducted. Primus Auditing Ops reserves the right not to publish the Audit Report if Customer has any outstanding debt.

9. CONFIDENTIALITY. . Primus Auditing Ops hereby represents and agrees that all information obtained or developed in connection with any audit performed under this Agreement, and for any audit performed for social compliance or otherwise governed by APSCA shall be kept confidential and shall not be disclosed to any party other than Customer, except in the following circumstances:
Customer requests and/or authorizes Primus Auditing Ops, in writing, to release such information to a specific third party; or
Where disclosure of such information to a third party is required in order for Primus Auditing Ops to perform and execute the services under this Agreement; or,
Primus Auditing Ops is required, pursuant to applicable and governing laws or regulation (by deposition, interrogatories, requests for information or documents in legal proceedings, subpoena, civil investigative demand or similar process), to disclose any or all of such obtained information; and in such case, only to the extent required by law; or,
Disclosure of such obtained information is required by Primus Auditing Ops to obtain legal or ethical advice regarding compliance with applicable laws, applicable codes and/or standards. Where confidentiality is not governed by a recognized professional code of conduct, an appropriate non-disclosure agreement must be executed by the third party prior to disclosure of such information; or,
Disclosure is required to establish a claim or defense by Primus Auditing Ops in an adversarial proceeding.

ul.li: Termination for Cause. This Service Agreement shall be indefinite, ending upon the publication of the Audit Report, or, if a Corrective Action Review is requested, upon the conclusion of the Corrective Action Review. If either party fails to fulfill any term or condition of this Agreement, such failure shall be considered a breach of this Agreement. The breaching party shall have 10 calendar days from the time of receipt of written notice from the other party to cure such breach. If after 10 days, the breaching party has not cured the breach, the non-breaching party may terminate this Agreement with no further obligations. The 10-day notice provision and termination is not applicable to violation of the Trademark use, as described in Section 13 herein - where the cure time upon notice will be 15 days.

Voluntary Termination. Either party may voluntarily terminate this Agreement upon fifteen days' written notice to the other party. If this Agreement is terminated by either party, all certifications granted by Primus Audit Ops to Customer after such termination shall not be valid.

Audits performed by Mexico Office. For all Audits scheduled with and performed by the Primus Auditing Ops office in Mexico, Customer agrees it shall pay the total audit fees prior to the scheduling and performance of the Audit. The total audit fee may include, but not limited to audit fee, admin fees, report entry times, travel time, evidence review, and travel expenses. Primus Auditing Ops will not schedule or perform any audit under this Agreement prior to receipt of full payment for audit fees.

Audits Conducted by the U.S. Offices. For all audits scheduled and conducted by the Primus Auditing Ops offices in the United States of America, the Client agrees to pay 750 USD prior to the scheduling and execution of the audit. The total audit fees may include, but are not limited to, audit fees, administrative fees, report entry time, travel time, evidence review, and travel expenses.

Audits Conducted by the Costa Rica Offices. For all audits scheduled and conducted by the Primus Auditing Ops offices in Costa Rica, the Client agrees to pay 50% of the total audit fees prior to the scheduling and execution of the audit. The total audit fees may include, but are not limited to, audit fees, administrative fees, report entry time, travel time, evidence review, and travel expenses.

Audits Conducted by the Chile Offices. For audits scheduled and conducted by the Chile office, the payment term must be 30 days after the invoice has been issued.
The Client agrees to pay Primus Auditing Ops the remaining balance within 30 days of receiving the invoice from Primus Auditing Ops for the outstanding amount. The total audit fees may include, but are not limited to, audit fees, administrative fees, report entry time, travel time, evidence review, and travel expenses.

div.p:
12. CANCELLATION FEES. If the client cancels or reschedules a scheduled audit date, they acknowledge, understand, and accept that they will be responsible for all non-refundable travel costs incurred by Primus Auditing Ops in connection with that audit. Additionally, any change or cancellation of an audit by the client will be subject to the following conditions, depending on the country where the audit is to be conducted. If, on the day of the audit, the auditor or any representative of Primus Auditing Ops is denied access to the field, facilities, or any area necessary to conduct the audit, the client acknowledges, understands, and accepts that they will be responsible for all quoted audit fees, in addition to all travel costs. In cases where access is completely denied at the time of the audit or if the audit is canceled within 24 hours prior to the audit or the start of the audit window—meaning the site does not allow the auditor to enter despite having a confirmed audit, regardless of the audit type (announced, semi-announced, or unannounced)—the total audit costs must be covered 100% as per the quoted amount.
For semi-announced or unannounced audits, if the audit is canceled or the requesting party requests changes after the audit window has started, a fee of 50% of the audit cost plus any incurred travel expenses will be charged.

Audits Conducted by the U.S. Offices
Any change or cancellation that occurs within 15 business days prior to the scheduled and/or confirmed audit date, as applicable, will result in a cancellation fee of 50% of the audit cost plus any incurred travel expenses.

Audits Conducted by the Chile Offices
Any change or cancellation that occurs within 15 business days prior to the scheduled and/or confirmed audit date, as applicable, will result in a cancellation fee of $400 USD plus any incurred travel expenses after the service has been confirmed.

Audits Conducted by the Costa Rica Offices
Any change or cancellation that occurs within 15 business days prior to the scheduled and/or confirmed audit date, as applicable, will result in a cancellation fee of 100% of the audit cost plus any incurred travel expenses after the service has been confirmed.

Audits Conducted by the Mexico Office
Any change or cancellation that occurs within 10 calendar days prior to the scheduled and/or confirmed audit date, as applicable, will result in a cancellation fee of $400 USD plus any incurred travel expenses.
Any change or cancellation that occurs within 5 calendar days prior to the scheduled and/or confirmed audit date, as applicable, will result in a cancellation fee of 50% of the audit cost plus any incurred travel expenses.

13. LOGO and URN. The guidelines for the usage of the SEDEX Member Logo can be found on their website (www.sedex.com) and in the document titled SEDEX Ambassador toolkit. The Customer must not misuse the SMETA report and CAPR.

The acceptance of these Terms and Conditions can be done through Oddo, PDF, or other electronic signature means. Primus Auditing Ops' electronic, digital, or printed copies of these Terms and Conditions, Customer's acceptance, and Quotes signed or otherwise accepted by Customer will be true, complete, valid, authentic, and enforceable copies of these documents. Customer agrees not to challenge the admissibility or enforceability of Primus Auditing Ops' copies in a court or in any proceeding arising from such documents.
